messages:
olivia: procurement sent over quotes from LedgerFlow and MatchLedger for invoice automation. pricing models look apples vs oranges. anyone quick familiarity?
harry: LedgerFlow did a POC with us last year. solid extractor, but they charge per-extracted-field which got messy.
maya: MatchLedger's sheet is weird: flat per-invoice but additional charge for "reconciliation events" (per mismatch).
finance-ops: Key constraints: line-item level outputs, S3/webhook export, 7y audit logs, KMS support, processing SLA <4h for daily batches.
harry: LedgerFlow excerpt: "$0.08 per invoice + $0.004 per extracted field; attachments $0.01/page. min commit $30k/yr. includes SSO."
omaya: MatchLedger excerpt: "$0.06 per invoice, $0.02 per reconciliation event (unmatched line or credit note), attachments waived via S3. min commit $45k/yr."
olivia: the per-reconciliation event metric seems risky for us since our unmatched rate is non-zero during onboarding. need sample cost at projected 1.2M/yr.
finance-ops: add to vendor questions: 1) does per-invoice include full line-level tax/discount/FX details? 2) how are nested line items counted? 3) provide monthly cost spreadsheet at 50k/150k/300k tiers and worst-case line counts.
harry: also ask for exportability of GL mapping rules (YAML/JSON) and versioning/rollback. if they won't export rules, it's a blocker.
procurement-bot: Reminder: attach RFP + sample BigQuery export when replying. Use /procure/reply-template-v2.
maya: suggested negotiation levers: cap monthly effective rate (e.g., don't charge > $0.05/effective invoice), include 40h PS in year 1, waive per-page fees for S3 uploads, and a credits schedule tied to acceptance accuracy.
olivia: I'll consolidate questions and send tonight. please review before I hit send. tagging @harry @maya @finance-ops. :rocket:
